author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Alexander Zverev advanced to the U.S. Open final Friday with a 6-3, 7-6(7), 7-6(6) victory over Karen Khachanov. The top seed controlled the opening set and survived two close tiebreaks to reach his third consecutive Grand Slam final and his second championship match at Flushing Meadows.

Zverev needed five sets in each of his first two matches in New York, but his tournament changed after that difficult start. He has now won four straight matches without dropping a set. The victory improved his 2026 record at major tournaments to 24-2 and moved the reigning French Open champion within one win of a second Grand Slam title.

Sunday's final will match Zverev against the winner of the all-American semifinal between Frances Tiafoe and Ben Shelton. Zverev's previous U.S. Open final came in 2020, when he lost to Dominic Thiem after taking a two-set lead in a stadium closed to spectators during the pandemic. This time he will face a sold-out Arthur Ashe Stadium and, potentially, a crowd strongly backing an American opponent.
dek: The French Open champion beat Karen Khachanov in straight sets and will play for his second major title Sunday.
headline: Zverev reaches U.S. Open final without dropping a set in four matches
